references.text: Moses gave instructions that Israel should only sacrifice at the place the Lord had chosen, which explains why the tribes reacted to the altar by the Jordan.
Instructions to build an altar of uncut stones on Mount Ebal, showing that altar building was regulated by God's law.
Israel crossed the Jordan and set up stones at Gilgal as a memorial, demonstrating the tradition of erecting monuments by the Jordan.
The other tribes heard about the altar and gathered for war, illustrating the direct consequence of the altar construction mentioned in verse 10.
Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh explained that the altar was intended as a witness, not for sacrifice, providing context for why they built it.
The tent of meeting was set up at Shiloh, which was the central place of worship, explaining why an alternative altar was problematic.
Israel built an altar at Bethel during the civil war against Benjamin, showing another situation involving altar construction in the land of Canaan.
